name: Taiga / coniferous forest
notes: Boreal coniferous forest: spruce, fir, pine and larch canopy over feathermoss, lichen and ericaceous dwarf shrubs. Eurasian (Norway spruce, Scots pine, Siberian larch) and North American (black/white spruce, balsam fir, jack pine) variants included.

canopy.name: Spruce
canopy.source: Picea abies (Norway spruce), Scandinavia to Urals, dominant boreal conifer 20-50 m, narrow conical crown

canopy.name: Black spruce
canopy.source: Picea mariana, Canada/Alaska boreal muskeg and uplands, narrow spire crown 5-20 m, dominant N American taiga tree

canopy.name: Fir
canopy.source: Abies balsamea, eastern Canada/NE USA boreal forest, dense conical fir 12-25 m, smooth grey bark

canopy.name: Larch
canopy.source: Larix sibirica, western Siberia/Urals, deciduous conifer 20-45 m, golden in autumn; vast light taiga stands

canopy.name: Scots pine
canopy.source: Pinus sylvestris, Scotland to Siberia, dry sandy boreal sites, 15-35 m with orange upper bark and flat crown

canopy.name: Paper birch
canopy.source: Betula papyrifera, Canada/Alaska boreal, pioneer after fire, white bark 15-25 m; Betula pendula fills the Eurasian role

shrub.name: Dwarf birch
shrub.source: Betula nana, boreal bogs and open taiga, 0.3-1.2 m

shrub.name: Labrador tea
shrub.source: Rhododendron groenlandicum, N American boreal bogs and black spruce forest, evergreen shrub 0.3-1 m with white flower clusters

shrub.name: Taiga willow
shrub.source: Salix bebbiana, N American boreal wet margins and clearings, 2-6 m shrub willow

shrub.name: Juniper
shrub.source: Juniperus communis, circumboreal open pine forest and rocky ground, spreading evergreen shrub 0.5-3 m

shrub.name: Bilberry
shrub.source: Vaccinium myrtillus, dominant field layer of Eurasian spruce/pine taiga, 20-60 cm deciduous dwarf shrub

ground.name: Lingonberry
ground.source: Vaccinium vitis-idaea, circumboreal pine/spruce forest floor, evergreen mat 10-30 cm with red berries

ground.name: Reindeer lichen
ground.source: Cladonia rangiferina, dominant ground cover of dry lichen pine woodland across boreal zone

ground.name: Rusty bog-moss
ground.source: Sphagnum fuscum, hummock peat moss of boreal bogs and black-spruce muskeg

ground.name: Feather moss
ground.source: Pleurozium schreberi (red-stemmed feathermoss), dominant carpet moss of closed spruce/pine taiga worldwide

ground.name: Fireweed
ground.source: Chamaenerion angustifolium, circumboreal burns and clearings, magenta flower spikes 0.5-2 m
